the extent to which industrial relations systems in western Europe are undergoing fundamental transformation.

the industrial relations systems of western Europe are in a state of considerable flux, with no clear direction.
the industrial relations of Western Europe have entered an era of ambiguity, in which the old patterns are being eroded and the new patterns are not yet established.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the industrial relations of Western Europe have been characterized by a period of considerable ambiguity.
the industrial relations systems of the 1980's are characterized by ambiguity and ambivalence.

, in the 1980's, the institutional framework of industrial relations has been challenged in most western European countries, and that the challenges have been met by a mixture of adaptation and resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the industrial relations systems of western Europe are not converging, but rather are becoming increasingly differentiated.
the 1980's and early 1990's were a period of ambiguity in industrial relations in Western Europe, not a period of convergence.
